feed.title: Combined summary - Libshrincs: A C implementation with a machine-checked security proof

entry.title: Combined summary - Libshrincs: A C implementation with a machine-checked security proof
entry.summary: The development of libshrincs marks a substantial advancement in cryptographic libraries designed for Bitcoin, particularly through its C-based implementation of the WOTS+C one-time signature scheme. By integrating machine-checked proofs, the project ensures both the functional correctness and security of its cryptographic operations. Public availability on [GitHub](https://github.com/remix7531/libshrincs) encourages transparency and collaboration, allowing for open peer review and community contributions. The use of advanced verification tools such as Rocq Prover and SSProve automates proof validation processes, reducing manual verification efforts and enhancing the reliability of the library. Central to libshrincs is the synergy between formal verification tools and practical software engineering. The Verified Software Toolchain (VST) meticulously aligns the C codebase with formal specifications defined in Rocq, while SSProve articulates and verifies the security guarantees of the implementation. This rigorous approach not only strengthens the trustworthiness of the library but also sets a methodological precedent for future cryptographic projects. To make these sophisticated verification techniques accessible, the project team has produced an in-depth tutorial ([PDF](https://github.com/remix7531/libshrincs/blob/0c572e747430af5a4fa7ddd7d3089fdffeb59d7d/docs/SSPROVE_SECURITY_REVIEW.pdf)) that guides reviewers from foundational concepts to complex security considerations, fostering broader engagement with formal methods. Despite the robust design, the current security theorem underlying libshrincs does not fully address post-quantum adversarial threats. The limitations are partially attributed to the absence of comprehensive models that encapsulate quantum attack scenarios. Addressing these gaps would require more elaborate proofs and adjustments to existing assumptions, especially within the quantum random oracle model. Nevertheless, the project's evolution was notably accelerated by leveraging large language models (LLMs), which aided in swiftly generating and iterating formal proofs. This collaboration between human expertise and artificial intelligence exemplifies how future cryptographic systems can benefit from such partnerships, potentially making formal verification a standard practice in secure software design. A series of blog posts authored by @remix7531 provides extensive documentation and reflection on the creation and refinement of libshrincs. The introductory post, ["Towards libshrincs"](https://remix7531.com/post/towards-libshrincs/), outlines the motivations and guiding principles behind the project’s inception, offering valuable context for understanding its objectives. In ["The grind was the only detector"](https://remix7531.com/post/the_grind_was_the_only_detector/), the challenges faced during development are candidly discussed, emphasizing the importance of perseverance and rigorous testing in complex software projects. Finally, ["Choosing a verification toolchain"](https://remix7531.com/post/choosing_a_verification_toolchain/) explores the reasoning and criteria involved in selecting appropriate tools for reliable and efficient verification, serving as a resource for developers confronting similar choices. From a compositional perspective, particular attention must be paid to the SHRINCS boundary conditions, where the gap between the proved experiment and standard one-time EUF-CMA becomes significant. Ensuring that the digest is fixed before exposing the WOTS public key and preventing state rollback that could lead to key reuse are critical requirements. Developing a composition argument that addresses these conditions would greatly clarify the security assurances of SHRINCS usage, enhancing both confidence in and understanding of the system’s robustness. Overall, libshrincs stands as a pioneering example of combining formal verification with practical cryptographic software implementation. The methodologies and tools employed elevate the standards for security and reliability in cryptographic libraries, paving the way for safer digital interactions and inspiring ongoing innovation in the field.
